classes.post: One-way op, sent in call order on the control channel; returns at once. A Swift caller that binds, guards, compares or returns the result is refused (--check-return-use) unless the site is a host_mode_rewrites entry. pending_keys name the mirror keys it changes: pending (or optimistic) until the host's ack (task 016b). Like a one-way mojo message.
classes.mirror: Served on main from the client's cache, which the host's MIRROR pushes refresh in the same per-frame batch as the events in refresh_events, pushed before those events (tasks 013 and 016b). Chrome caches the renderer's pushed TextInputState the same way and answers NSTextInputClient queries from it (content/browser/renderer_host/text_input_manager.cc). A read before attach is a bug: the client returns the C zero value (0 or NULL) and reports a fault (task 014). In host mode CEFRuntime.start awaits attach before its first shim call (task 015), so the startup reads listed in host_mode_rewrites (needs after_attach) see the host's hello; --check-pre-attach (task 011) refuses any other mirror read on the startup path before that await.
classes.async: Sent with a token; the answer is reply_event, resumed by token (task 018). The remote returns at once (1 once sent, NULL for a string result) and cmux_remote_shim_last_reply_token(), read right after the call, is the token of its wire:REPLY: the result, then the out-parameters. CEFHostStart.expectReply() reads it in the call's turn and expects it in CEFHostStart.replies (CEFHostReplies, CEFS/CEFReplyWaiters.swift, one per runtime), which awaits it with an injected-clock deadline. The remote shim's reply callback (cmux_remote_shim_set_reply, main thread) only copies the bytes in; the typed decode (CEFHostReplyFields) runs off main in the awaiting call. Every pending token resolves with .hostGone when the host exits (task 091). Like a mojo method with a reply callback; never a [Sync] call.
classes.mint: The client mints the id (browser ids in [1 << 20, 1 << 30), DevTools message ids below 2^30); the host maps it to Chromium's id for every op and event (task 019, HOST/src/host_client_ids.h). The C return keeps the header's contract, named by mint_returns: id returns the minted id at once; sent returns 1 when the op is sent, and the minted id first reaches cmux in reply_event. A browser the host's shim refuses comes as CMUX_SHIM_CREATE_FAILED. In process, AFTER_CREATED runs inside the call; in host mode it comes in a later batch, so a Swift site that relies on that order is a host_mode_rewrites entry. A tab Chromium opens for a window request (a popup, target=_blank, chrome.windows.create) gets an id the host mints from 1 << 30 when its shim decides the request with cmux's pushed policy (task 031): CMUX_SHIM_WINDOW_REQUEST_RESULT carries it before the tab exists and the tab's AFTER_CREATED names it by it (HOST/src/host_window_request_ids.h). Other tabs Chromium opens itself (DevTools browsers) keep Chromium's id, the same number on both sides.
classes.policy: A synchronous callback becomes a policy pushed to the host plus events; the host decides inside Chromium without asking cmux (tasks 030-033).
classes.view: NSView* or page-window plumbing: ChromiumHostPageView owns it in host mode, where cmux passes the page view's token for an NSView* argument (CEFRuntime.mintPageViewToken) and the client sends it as is; only geometry and ids cross the wire (tasks 040, 052, 053, 066).
classes.local: Function-pointer args or client-only work: hand-written client code (task 014b), no generated marshaller.
classes.preinit: Queued in the client until the host attaches and applied in call order before CefInitialize (task 013); a call after initialize is sent as a post. Like calls on a mojo Remote before its pipe is bound (mojo/public/cpp/bindings/remote.h). A non-void preinit returns at once the client's own check (1 when queued, 0 for an argument the header refuses, such as a reserved scheme id or an empty path); the host's verdict is reply_event wire:REPLY, sent when it applies the op and handled off main by token. --check-return-use covers preinit as it covers post, so a Swift caller that reads the result is a host_mode_rewrites entry.

fields.name: The export, as in the header.
fields.class: One of classes. There is no sync class.
fields.args: Parameters in header order: name, C type, function_pointer true for a callback.
fields.result_used_by: Files under sources_root whose call sites use the result today (a census; --check-return-use computes the live list).
fields.mirror_key: mirror only: scope.field[key args]; the key args name the export's parameters.
fields.refresh_events: mirror only: event kinds whose batch refreshes the key; CMUX_SHIM_TAB_EVENT:<n> names a tab event sub-kind; attach is the host's hello.
fields.pending_keys: post only: mirror keys the op changes; * stands for a key arg the op does not name.
fields.mint_returns: mint only: id (the C return is the minted id) or sent (1 when sent; the minted id arrives in reply_event).
fields.reply_event: The event kind, or wire:REPLY (the control channel's reply frame with the return value and outputs), that answers the call; for a non-void preinit, the host's verdict when it applies the op.
fields.channel: Optional: input for ops sent on the input ring instead of the control channel (default control).
fields.optional_exports: Top level: cmux_shim_* symbols CEFShimLibrary binds with r.optional (the fork API 29 renderer paths) that cmux_cef_shim.h does not declare. 3696a48e40a landed the app side before the shim, and the shim in CEFShim/src does not define them yet, so a declaration would promise symbols that nm cannot find in the real shim. Same fields as exports. Task 011 checks header exports plus these against CEFShimLibrary's r(...) and r.optional(...) names; the remote dylib (task 014) exports both. The commit that adds them to the shim moves the declarations into the header and these entries into exports.
fields.optional_events: Top level: event kinds CEFShimEvent.swift decodes that cmux_shim_event_kind_t does not list yet (fork API 29); same fields as events and the same move into the header as optional_exports.
fields.host_mode_rewrites: Top level: Swift sites whose in-process behavior the remote shim cannot keep, and sites that stay as written in host mode: site (file and function under sources_root), exports, needs (after_attach, reply, pending_tab, host_exit, or kept: the site stays, change says why; a finished pending_tab site becomes kept), change, and task. --check-return-use and --check-pre-attach (task 011) accept a site only while it is listed here. --swift-sites (task 021) no longer lists a site listed with after_attach, host_exit or kept, nor an async call in the token form (a closure handed to CEFRuntime.sendAsync, siteCall or profileWrite), nor a mint_returns id call in the mint form (its id keys the wait for its reply_event).

pseudo_events.attach: The host's hello after the control channel connects, before any op is applied. It carries every mirror key whose only refresh event is attach, and the optional_exports the host's shim defines.
